sections.h2: How do Auburn Hills' rental and vacancy rules touch a home sale?
sections.html:
They matter whenever a buyer plans to rent the house or when the house sits empty before closing. The city's Community Development Department registers every detached one-family home that is rented or offered for rent, and it keeps a separate registry for vacant homes.

  • Rental registration costs $200, the permit to occupy $50, and the yearly renewal $250, due December 31.
  • Instead of filing a self-certification checklist, an owner can pay $155 for a city interior inspection.
  • A $100 penalty applies to a first failure to register, and civil infraction tickets can follow.
  • A buyer of an existing rental has 30 days from the sale to register again and obtain a new permit.
  • A vacant home must be registered within 30 days, and the vacant-home form lists a $355 fee.

A letter from the city about registering does not prove you are renting, because the city targets homes not claimed as a homestead. Return a Statement of Exemption for a non-rental home and no fee applies. Even a house where a relative lives rent-free can count as a rental. Community Development is at 1827 N. Squirrel Road, phone 248-364-6900.

sections.h2: Where did Auburn Hills come from?
sections.html:
The city is young on paper and old on the map. It was created in 1983 when Pontiac Township merged with the village of Auburn Heights, though settlement on the Clinton River goes back to 1821, when a sawmill and grist mill drew families to the village of Auburn.

The village faded after the 1860s and was renamed Amy in 1880, then Auburn Heights in 1919. In 1908 automobile pioneer John Dodge bought a farmhouse northeast of the village, and the land he and his wife accumulated grew to 1,400 acres. In 1957 the family donated acreage that became Oakland University. A neighboring country estate, bought by the township in 1975, now serves as the Civic Center.

State officials rejected a 1971 attempt to incorporate as Pontiac Heights. The township became a charter township in 1978 to guard against annexation, and the merger followed five years later. Oakland Community College gave the name Auburn Hills to its campus in 1964, at a former Nike missile base.

Downtown Auburn Hills traces to 2002, when the corner of Auburn and Squirrel roads was revived as the Village Center with new streetscape. By the end of 2013 it had gained a four-story graduate student apartment building, a 233-space parking deck, a University Center for college classes and a restored log cabin that serves as a student and community center. The Seyburn estate that became the Civic Center once had stables, kennels, a swimming pool and a 5,000 square foot Colonial Revival house.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Auburn Hills?
sections.html:
Automotive firms dominate. More than 50 automotive corporations run facilities here, Stellantis keeps its North American headquarters in the city, and the tech and office buildings hold about 80,000 people on a workday.

Other names on the employer list include BorgWarner, PHINIA, Guardian Industries, Autoliv, Joyson Safety Systems, GKN Driveline and Faurecia, plus the North American headquarters of Volkswagen and Audi. Maserati moved its U.S. headquarters into the former Walter P. Chrysler Museum building in 2017. The Oakland Technology Park was approved in 1985, and Great Lakes Crossing Outlets opened on November 12, 1998. The Palace of Auburn Hills, home of the Detroit Pistons, has been demolished.

For residents age 16 and over, 69.9 percent are in the labor force and the mean commute is 22.1 minutes. Those jobs sit a short drive from most houses in the city, and a seller can lean on that in a listing.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Auburn Hills housing?
sections.html:
Owners occupy 51.3 percent of homes and renters the rest, and households run small, at 2.10 people on average.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks come with an Auburn Hills address?
sections.html:
Three districts serve the city: Avondale, Pontiac and Rochester Community Schools. Avondale runs Graham and Auburn elementary schools inside the city limits, the district offices and a Montessori program, and every Avondale resident is zoned to Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. A Pontiac school, Will Rogers Elementary, sits in the northeast corner. Auburn Hills Christian School and Oakland Christian School are private options.

Buyers also look at parks and trails:

  • The Civic Center Park has nature trails, a fishing pond, a softball field, tennis courts and a nine-hole disc golf course.
  • The free skate park is open from April to November.
  • A 2.1 mile crushed stone stretch of the 16-mile Clinton River Trail crosses the city.

Oakland University and Oakland Community College both have campuses here, and the Auburn Hills Public Library is a local draw.

sections.h2: What does it take to record an Auburn Hills deed in Oakland County?
sections.html:
The Oakland County Register of Deeds records it, and any warranty deed, land contract or deed with a warranty clause needs a stamp from the Oakland County Treasurer first. The office takes calls at 248-858-0597 on weekdays.

State and county transfer taxes together equal $8.60 per $1,000. On a $245,000 sale, the median value in the city, that comes to $2,107, charged to the seller. Because Oakland is a charter county, ask the office for its current recording fee.

Electronic recording works through approved vendors. The county's MiPropDocs tool excludes deeds, which transfer ownership, so a deed goes through a vendor or the office counter.

sections.h2: What does the Auburn Hills assessor need after a sale?
sections.html:
The buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit within 45 days, with $5 a day charged for late residential filings up to $200. The assessor works weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Michigan counts property status on tax day, December 31 of the prior year. Assessed value is half of true cash value, and taxable value is the lesser of state equalized value and the capped value. The cap grows with inflation or 5 percent, whichever is lower, until ownership changes.

  • Sellers rescind their exemption on the old home with Form 2602, within 90 days of moving out.
  • Buyers who move in before the May 1 deadline claim theirs with Form 2368.
  • A buyer moving in between June 2 and November 1 can claim it for winter taxes that year.

Closing agents are expected to bring both forms, though the law gives no remedy if one forgets.

faqs.q: Is there a required pre-sale inspection in Auburn Hills?
faqs.a: The city's published rules center on rental and vacant home registration. Ask Community Development at 248-364-6900 whether any step applies to your house before you pick a closing date.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a $245,000 Auburn Hills sale?
faqs.a: It is $2,107, at $8.60 per $1,000, and the seller pays it. The state takes $3.75 per $500 and the county takes 55 cents per $500.

faqs.q: What happens to rental registration when an Auburn Hills rental sells?
faqs.a: The buyer registers again and gets a new permit to occupy within 30 days, paying $200 for registration and $50 for the permit.

faqs.q: Which county records deeds for Auburn Hills?
faqs.a: Oakland County. The Register of Deeds records the deed, and warranty deeds need a county treasurer certification first.

faqs.q: How long does a buyer have to report the sale to the city assessor?
faqs.a: Forty-five days. A late residential filing costs $5 per day, capped at $200.
